newsitem.title: UK: Young doctors may flee Britain, study shows.
newsitem.headline: Young doctors may flee Britain, study shows.

text.p: Newly trained doctors may be planning to abandon Britain for greener pastures, or could give up medicine altogether, researchers warned on Friday.
They said a survey of just-trained doctors in 1993 showed more than ever seemed ambivalent about a career in Britain.
Trevor Lambert, a statistician at Oxford University, and colleagues surveyed 2,600 graduates and asked them whether they planned to practice in Britain.
They found 75 percent said yes. "This 1993 figure is lower than that for any cohort previously surveyed," they wrote in a report in the British Medical Journal (BMJ).

"Although early intentions do not inevitably correspond with future careers, the doctors' responses show an increased lack of commitment to a medical career in the United Kingdom, which may be an early warning of either higher loss of higher disenchantment in the future."
In an editorial the BMJ said the long hours and heavy workload of junior doctors in Britain could be partly to blame.
"Fortunately there is some evidence that the lot of young doctors is beginning to improve," it said.
"This is not before time; without sustained improvement the risk of doctors disappearing from medicine is real. Many are highly critical and disaffected."
